name: Israel
summary_text: Israel is the Middle East's most progressive destination for trans visitors, with no criminalisation, anti-discrimination protections, court-based legal gender recognition (with dead-name removal from IDs as of 2025), publicly funded transition healthcare, and Tel Aviv as a regional queer hub. Two traveler-specific risks pull the score down. First, Ben-Gurion Airport has no regulations for interacting with trans travelers — documented humiliating questioning and detainment, with surgery demanded for gender recognition ("If you don't undergo surgery, you're still a male"). Every foreign visitor transits Ben-Gurion, making this a high-probability friction point. Second, violence is rising sharply: 433 homophobic/transphobic physical incidents were reported in 2025, including dating-app traps and organized ambushes, with transgender people "bearing the brunt." Trump's anti-trans rhetoric is reportedly inflaming the local climate. The right-wing Netanyahu coalition and the Israel-Hamas war aftermath have weakened protections, though the National Security Committee has convened on LGBTQ public-space security.

sources.title: ‘If You Don’t Undergo Surgery, You’re Still a Male’: A Transgender Nightmare at Israeli Airport - Israel News
sources.claim_summary: Haaretz magazine (May 2023): 'A Transgender Nightmare at Israeli Airport' - Israel's Airports Authority has no regulations for interacting with trans travellers; trans people describe humiliating questioning and detention at Ben-Gurion Airport ('If you don't undergo surgery, you're still a male'). Directly documents airport-screening problems for trans travellers in Israel.

sources.title: Homophobic, transphobic violence rose in Israel in 2025, new data shows | The Jerusalem Post
sources.claim_summary: Jerusalem Post (May 2026): the Aguda's Nir Katz Center 2025 report found 432 homophobic or transphobic physical incidents in Israel in 2025 - a sharp rise, including 'carefully planned lynch ambushes carried out through dating apps', stabbings and extortion.

sources.title: Dating-app traps, organized ambushes: anti-LGBTQ violence hits record high in Israel
sources.claim_summary: Ynet (May 2026): Israel's 2025 LGBTQ-phobia report finds record-high anti-LGBTQ violence - at least one physical assault per week; physical attacks rose to half of public-space incidents (from 32%); extortion/threats rose from 3% to 13.5%; 91% of survey respondents experienced LGBTQ-phobia in the past year but only 7% reported it; trans people bear the brunt despite being a minority within the community.

sources.title: 'Very, Very Afraid': Trump's Inflammatory Rhetoric Is Impacting Israel's Transgender Community - Israel News
sources.claim_summary: Haaretz (Feb 2025): Trump's anti-trans rhetoric and executive orders are impacting Israel's transgender community - activists report increasing violent rhetoric locally, including transphobia from within the LGBTQ community.

sources.title: Israel Police Adopt New Regulation for Searching Trans People - Israel News
sources.claim_summary: Haaretz (May 2023): Israel Police issued a new regulation for body searches of trans people who have not fully transitioned - male officers will search male genitalia and female officers female genitalia; LGBTQ groups decry the regulation as harmful, humiliating and traumatic (previously officers had to ask the person's preference).

sources.title: Registration of previous name abolished for transgender people | The Jerusalem Post
sources.claim_summary: Jerusalem Post (June 2024): the Interior Ministry amended ID regulations so trans people no longer need to register their 'dead name' on their teudat zehut - following a High Court petition by trans woman Nofar Ashbel, who argued that displaying the previous name outed her gender change.
NOTE: Not retrievable at research time (HTTP 404 - page removed); the underlying page addressed trans rights in Israel - laws, protections and gaps.

sources.title: Israel | Outright International
sources.claim_summary: Outright International country overview (updated March 2026): no criminalisation since the 1988 repeal; anti-discrimination protections across statutes (2000 products/services law, Patient Rights Law, Student Rights Law - the latter also covering gender identity); conversion practices prohibited for medical professionals; same-sex marriages performed abroad registrable since 2006; joint adoption affirmed by the High Court in 2018.

Times of Israel: 'Most Israelis favor same-sex marriage, but half of MKs mum on issue' - a Channel 10 survey found majority public support for same-sex marriage while half of lawmakers declined to state a position, including a culture minister who has marched in the Pride parade.
